answer: A flute-maker's bore tuning keeps Sybils out. A newcomer tunes 12 flutes over 28 days. Each bore is sounded and pitch-checked within a quarter tone by two flute-makers from separate shops in 48 hours, each result logged in the register, line by line like a sonnet. One flute off pitch voids its credit and pauses tuning 14 days; three void the whole register. Faking 1,000 agents means 12,000 flutes and 24,000 checks, $180,000 in wages, while one honest agent just keeps tuning. A pearl forms only around a real grain of sand, and standing grows the same way, in a slow spiral of work done.
